name: Cascade-Correlation
summary: Starts with no hidden units, trains candidate units to correlate with residual error, adds the best candidate when residual-correlation search finds a useful feature, freezes its input weights, and repeats.

name: Growing Neural Gas
summary: Moves input-space prototypes, maintains competitive-Hebbian edges with local aging, and periodically inserts a prototype in the graph region with greatest accumulated squared-distance error; source-grounded details remain not human-reviewed.

name: Grow When Required
summary: Uses match activity and winner habituation to choose immediate prototype insertion or continued winner-and-neighbor adaptation while maintaining an aged neighborhood graph; source-grounded details remain not human-reviewed.

name: Dynamic Node Construction
summary: Expands a backpropagation network when normalized error progress over the current topology flattens, then continues ordinary backpropagation over old and new weights; the close read remains not human-reviewed.

name: Resource-Allocating Network
summary: Allocates a local unit only when an input is beyond the current distance scale and its output error exceeds desired accuracy; otherwise it refines output weights, offset, and centers.

name: Recurrent Cascade-Correlation
summary: Extends the cascade-correlation growth pattern into recurrent sequence-learning settings, while the reviewed 1995 analysis cautions that freezing or growth alone does not remove topology-imposed representational limits.

name: Constructive fully recurrent growth
summary: A cautious family label for approaches that add neurons during recurrent-network training while trying to preserve a fully recurrent topology rather than inheriting the one-directional cascade constraint.

name: Constructive spiking taxonomy
summary: Uses the thesis-derived three-process lens—when structure changes, what changes, and how parameters are chosen—to compare construction, pruning, and merging in spiking and non-spiking systems.

name: Evolving spiking-network lineage
summary: A cautious active-bundle bridge for eSNN/STDC material: Schliebs2013 grounds the lineage and vocabulary of evolving spiking networks, Wysoski2010 provides a reviewed audiovisual application anchor, Kasabov2013 is now the dynamic eSNN/deSNN detail-review placeholder, and Wang2014 is the supervised adaptive-structure placeholder. Exact growth-rule claims for Kasabov2013, Wang2014, and Roy2017 remain pending close full-text or human review.

name: Simulation expansion and contraction
summary: Interprets construction and pruning as transfers between simulated and surrounding neuron/synapse sets, with biological-plausibility constraints on how much activity a structural change may disrupt.

name: STDP hidden-pattern learning
summary: A cautious bundle-level bridge for the promoted STDP reviews: STDP can grow synaptic selectivity for repeated temporal structure, competition can make a fixed pool of listeners differentiate, single-neuron learnability results bound what timing-dependent synapse tuning can supply, and biological/phenomenological STDP reviews constrain how simple timing-window stories should be interpreted. This is not recorded as a neuron-growth algorithm until a reviewed source verifies structural growth.

name: Bottleneck adapter
summary: Adds a small down-project/nonlinearity/up-project module with an internal skip connection twice per Transformer layer, trains it plus new layer-norm parameters, and leaves the pre-trained weights fixed; details are automated readings and not human-reviewed.

name: LoRA (low-rank adaptation)
summary: Learns a rank-r product BA as the update to a frozen weight matrix, initializing B at zero so training starts from the base function, and can merge the delta into the weights so inference costs nothing extra; details are automated readings and not human-reviewed.

name: Mixture of LoRA Experts (MoLE)
summary: Treats each layer of each trained LoRA as an expert and learns only a per-layer gating function over them, keeping the base model and every LoRA frozen and allowing branches to be masked out at inference; details are automated readings and not human-reviewed.

name: Net2Net
summary: Widens a layer by replicating units and dividing their outgoing weights by the replication count, and deepens a network by inserting an identity-initialized layer, so the larger network starts from exactly the smaller one's function; details are automated readings and not human-reviewed.

name: G_stack depthwise stacking
summary: Initializes a deep model by composing a trained small model with itself g times and then continues pre-training; duplication carries the learned weights forward but preserves no function, and the reported optimal g lies between 2 and 4. Automated reading, not human-reviewed.

name: Progressive neural networks
summary: Adds a new column per task with lateral connections into every earlier column, freezing all earlier parameters so old tasks cannot be disturbed, at the cost of parameters that grow with the number of tasks; automated reading, not human-reviewed.

name: Product-key memory
summary: Uses two learned sub-key sets to retrieve a sparse weighted set of learned value rows from a very large implicit key space; automated reading, not human-reviewed.

name: Scaled memory layers
summary: Shares and parallelizes sparse key–value memory so dedicated capacity reaches a reported 128B parameters without activating the whole table; automated reading, not human-reviewed.

name: Sparse memory finetuning
summary: Ranks memory accesses against background usage and enables gradients only for top-t value slots; reduced interference is the paper’s reported result, not a guarantee. Automated reading, not human-reviewed.

name: Sparse autoencoder read-out
summary: Fits an auxiliary sparse feature dictionary over existing model activations and can clamp feature coordinates for steering; it reads and intervenes on existing activity rather than adding base-model capacity. Automated reading, not human-reviewed.
